question: A nurse wants to search for articles mentioning either 'pain' or 'discomfort'. Which search word should be used?

options.A: NOT
options.B: AND
options.C: WITH
options.D: OR

explanation: The word OR tells the database to look for either term, helping you catch helpful synonyms and expand your search.

question: Which virus from unsafe injections can survive on surfaces outside the body for at least seven days?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Ebola virus
options.D: Hepatitis C virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is very tough and can remain infectious on environmental surfaces for a week or more. Always treat gear with care!

question: Why do doctors order a D-dimer blood test when checking for a deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?

options.A: To look for protein fragments that show a recent blood clot is breaking down
options.B: To measure blood pressure inside leg veins
options.C: To see plaque buildup inside the aorta
options.D: To check how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: D-dimer is a leftover protein piece that floats around when the body is dissolving a blood clot. If the test is negative, it's a great clue that a clot isn't lurking there!

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Making people active partners in their own health
options.B: Allowing foreign donors to control local clinics
options.C: Reducing the cost of building government hospitals
options.D: Punishing communities that ignore public health advice

explanation: Community mobilisation shifts people from being passive receivers of care to active participants who help shape health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of using mobile outreach teams in immunization programs?

options.A: To sell prescription medications directly to rural households
options.B: To reach children living in remote or hard-to-access communities
options.C: To collect taxes from local markets on behalf of the government
options.D: To replace permanent primary health centers in major cities

explanation: You got it! Mobile teams bridge the gap so children in hard-to-reach areas don't miss out on life-saving vaccines.

question: What is the main job of the meninges in the body?

options.A: To connect peripheral nerves directly to bones
options.B: To pump oxygen-rich blood into the brain tissue
options.C: To produce most of the body's neurotransmitters
options.D: To protect and cushion the central nervous system

explanation: You've got this! The meninges are layers of tissue that wrap around the brain and spinal cord like a safety cushion to protect them from bumps and injuries.

question: Which room adjustment helps prevent falls on indoor steps for someone with low vision?

options.A: Removing the handrails to give more space for walking
options.B: Polishing the wooden steps until they are shiny and smooth
options.C: Installing dark-colored carpeting that blends with the floor
options.D: Placing bright, contrasting tape on the edge of each step

explanation: Great job! High-contrast markings make it much easier for the patient's eyes to catch where each step begins and ends.

question: A patient feels nervous and ashamed talking about past sexual partners during a clinic visit. What is the best way to handle this as a nurse?

options.A: Scold the patient for engaging in risky behaviors that threaten health
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to build trust and offer education
options.C: Refuse to discuss the topic further until a physician enters the room
options.D: Document the behavior as non-compliant in the permanent hospital record

explanation: You're a natural! Creating a safe, warm space builds trust and makes it easy for patients to share and learn. Keep up the daily habit—you're doing great!

question: What is the main idea behind social learning theory?

options.A: Building personal mental maps of human anatomy
options.B: Observing and imitating the actions of role models
options.C: Taking computer-based exams to test long-term memory
options.D: Receiving direct financial rewards for good test scores

explanation: We learn so much just by watching the people around us! Social learning proves we pick up habits by observing mentors and seeing what works for them.

question: What happens to the solid particles in a drug suspension over time?

options.A: Solid particles are dispersed and tend to settle
options.B: Solid particles are fully dissolved in the liquid
options.C: Active ingredients are bound permanently to the bottle
options.D: The mixture remains completely clear at all times

explanation: Think of muddy water! Suspensions have tiny bits of medicine floating around that love to sink to the bottom if left alone. That's why we always shake them first!

question: Which inventory rule ensures that medicines closer to their expiration date are used first?

options.A: Most-Expensive, First-Used
options.B: First-Expired, First-Out
options.C: Random-Selection Method
options.D: First-In, Last-Out

explanation: Correct! FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out) helps prevent waste and patient risk by making sure older stock gets used before new deliveries.

question: How do Standard Precautions differ from original Universal Precautions?

options.A: Standard Precautions remove the need for handwashing if gloves are worn
options.B: Standard Precautions apply to all body fluids and moist tissues, not just blood
options.C: Standard Precautions ignore non-intact skin and focus solely on respiratory droplets
options.D: Standard Precautions are only used when a patient has a confirmed laboratory diagnosis

explanation: While Universal Precautions focused mainly on blood, Standard Precautions broaden the safety net to include all body fluids, secretions, and non-intact skin for every patient. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: A doctor prescribes 3.0 mL of medication to be given subcutaneously. What should you do?

options.A: Split the dose and inject it into two different subcutaneous sites
options.B: Administer the full dose as a single subcutaneous injection
options.C: Call the doctor to question the volume and discuss alternative routes
options.D: Give the entire medication into the deltoid muscle instead

explanation: Spot on! 3.0 mL is way too much for one sub-Q site and would cause unnecessary pain and tissue damage. Always speak up and clarify with the prescriber.

question: Why must sublingual nitroglycerin tablets be stored in a special dark, airtight glass bottle?

options.A: Glass containers prevent the pills from melting in warm weather.
options.B: Light turns the medication into a dangerous poison.
options.C: The medication loses potency easily when exposed to light and air.
options.D: Dark bottles keep the tablets from sticking together.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin loses its strength quickly if light and air get to it, so the special bottle keeps it potent.

question: What type of room air pressure is needed for a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: Neutral pressure
options.B: Negative pressure
options.C: Positive pressure
options.D: Variable pressure

explanation: Spot on! Negative pressure acts like a trap, making sure air rushes inside when the door opens instead of leaking out into the hallway.

question: Which of these is NOT normal and actually represents a danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Passing dark green meconium poop on the first day
options.B: Grunting when breathing and chest sinking in
options.C: Spitting up a tiny bit of milk after feeding
options.D: Sleeping soundly between regular feeds

explanation: Chest retractions and grunting are red flags! They tell us the baby is working way too hard to breathe and needs urgent help.

question: Which activity is an effective way to reach a large group of people during a community mental health campaign?

options.A: Market square talks and radio awareness programs
options.B: Locking patients inside a quiet room
options.C: Destroying traditional medicine books
options.D: Waiting quietly at the clinic for someone to walk in

explanation: Reaching out through public spaces and mass media ensures that mental health messages reach everyday community members where they gather. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h7)

question: How does poor hospital infrastructure affect a nurse's daily shift?

options.A: It forces nurses to spend more time improvising care due to missing tools
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will receive higher hazard allowances
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients seeking medical attention
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for patient documentation

explanation: Nigerian nurses are masters of improvisation! When basic equipment is missing, you have to think on your feet to keep patients safe. That takes true skill.

question: A nurse manager suddenly sees patient admissions double overnight. Which budgeting phase does this affect the most?

options.A: Historical auditing of past years
options.B: Initial executive board selection
options.C: Implementation and monitoring
options.D: Capital equipment depreciation

explanation: This happens during the live implementation phase, where managers constantly watch real-time patient numbers and adjust on the fly!

question: Why must healthcare resources always be carefully managed and rationed?

options.A: Governments prefer to spend money on education instead of health
options.B: Patients rarely use the medical services provided to them
options.C: Medical equipment is always too expensive to manufacture
options.D: Resources are limited while human healthcare needs are infinite

explanation: You'll see this a lot in practice: money, beds, and staff are finite, but sick patients always need care. That gap means we have to make smart choices! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing one's diet?

options.A: Cultural food traditions that conflict with medical diets
options.B: Possessing a strong personal desire to cook healthy meals
options.C: Lack of knowledge regarding food preparation skills
options.D: Financial constraints and the high cost of healthy food

explanation: Exactly! Wanting to cook healthy meals helps you succeed—it's a motivator, not a roadblock.

question: When reading a Mantoux test, what part of the skin reaction do you actually measure?

options.A: The hard, raised area of tissue known as induration
options.B: The dark bruising caused by the needle puncture
options.C: The total diameter of visible surface redness
options.D: The size of the initial wheal left after the injection

explanation: Don't measure the redness! Feel for the edges of that firm, hard bump underneath (the induration)—that's what tells the real story. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h5)

question: Which heart chamber is responsible for pumping freshly oxygenated blood out to the rest of the newborn's body?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the aorta to supply the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to healthy eating in low-resource settings?

options.A: Cultural beliefs restricting certain foods during illness
options.B: Poverty and rising market prices for fresh produce
options.C: Guaranteed year-round access to free imported organic foods
options.D: Lack of proper refrigeration and food storage facilities

explanation: Spot on! Free, imported organic foods are definitely not a common everyday reality for most people.

question: Why is keeping a close eye on food handlers such a big deal for public health?

options.A: It guarantees that restaurants make a high financial profit
options.B: It reduces the amount of spoiled food thrown away in kitchens
options.C: It speeds up the time it takes to cook meals for customers
options.D: It stops infected workers from causing widespread foodborne illness outbreaks

explanation: Because food handlers prepare meals for many people, proper oversight stops germs from spreading quickly to the public. Excellent thinking!

question: Which blood vessel brings oxygen-rich blood *back* from the placenta to the baby?

options.A: Spiral artery
options.B: Endometrial vein
options.C: Umbilical vein
options.D: Umbilical artery

explanation: A little clinical trick: just like veins in our body normally carry blood back to the heart, the umbilical *vein* carries fresh, oxygenated blood from the placenta to the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why is training in adolescent psychology helpful for nurses?

options.A: It guarantees higher government salaries
options.B: It allows nurses to prescribe adult psychiatric drugs
options.C: It replaces the need for physical examinations
options.D: It helps providers communicate effectively without personal biases

explanation: Correct! Good training helps us handle sensitive youth issues with empathy and professionalism, leaving personal judgment at the door.

question: Why is building a trusting relationship important during continuing care?

options.A: It legally binds the patient to live at the clinic
options.B: It keeps the patient engaged and compliant with their treatment plan
options.C: it stops family members from getting involved in care
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid documenting patient interactions

explanation: Trust makes patients feel safe sharing their true feelings and concerns, which helps prevent them from dropping out of care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: A patient is prescribed a new synergistic drug combo. What is a key nursing duty before giving it?

options.A: Restricting the patient from drinking any water for 24 hours
options.B: Telling the patient they can double the dose if pain increases
options.C: Checking baseline organ function tests and verify correct dosing
options.D: Stopping all other routine medications without physician approval

explanation: As a sharp nurse, you always check baseline labs like kidney and liver function first to make sure the patient can safely handle the combination.

question: What is another name for the body's specific defense system?

options.A: Adaptive immune system
options.B: Innate barrier response
options.C: Non-specific defense network
options.D: Mechanical protection layer

explanation: We call them specific defences the adaptive immune system because they adapt and target exact germs over time. You've got this!

question: A mosquito develops through an egg, larva, pupa, and winged adult. Which type of metamorphosis does this represent?

options.A: Simple metamorphosis
options.B: Incomplete metamorphosis
options.C: Complete metamorphosis
options.D: Direct development

explanation: Because it features four separate stages including a resting pupa, it is classified as complete metamorphosis. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h3)

question: What is the best nursing action when you spot a potential drug interaction on a patient's chart?

options.A: Administer the medications at the exact same time to save nursing time
options.B: Consult the prescriber or pharmacist to discuss a safer alternative or dosage adjustment
options.C: Stop all of the patient's home medications permanently without telling anyone
options.D: Wait until the patient develops physical symptoms before taking action

explanation: Always put patient safety first! As a nurse, you are a key safety barrier—collaborate with your pharmacist or doctor to sort out any red flags before giving the drugs.

question: What major global health target was famously set by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Eradication of all infectious diseases by 1985
options.B: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.C: Privatization of all national health sectors
options.D: Free tertiary hospital care for every global citizen

explanation: Alma-Ata made history by rallying the world around the bold dream of 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary care.

question: What should a nurse typically do after a patient gets a positive result on a screening RDT?

options.A: Start major surgery immediately
options.B: Throw away all the remaining test kits
options.C: Ignore the result and send the patient home
options.D: Perform a confirmatory test if required by guidelines

explanation: Screening tests can sometimes give false positives, so important diagnoses often require a second confirmatory test. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: How does prevention differ from traditional treatment in nursing?

options.A: Prevention stops illness before it starts, while treatment fixes existing problems
options.B: Prevention happens in hospitals, while treatment happens at home
options.C: Prevention uses only medication, while treatment uses talk therapy
options.D: Prevention is only done by doctors, while treatment is done by nurses

explanation: Prevention aims to intercept risk factors before a disorder develops, whereas traditional treatment addresses illness that is already present. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of a hierarchical communication barrier?

options.A: A junior nurse being too intimidated to report a abnormal sign to a senior doctor
options.B: A nurse misunderstanding a medical term written in a foreign language
options.C: A noisy infusion pump beeping loudly in a crowded intensive care unit
options.D: A tired staff member forgetting to read the morning shift handover notes

explanation: Fear of authority and strict power gaps create hierarchical barriers that prevent vital patient safety information from traveling upward. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h4)

question: Which clinical situation is best suited for the reverse Trendelenburg position (head higher than feet)?

options.A: Performing a routine rectal examination
options.B: Treating sudden low blood pressure after trauma
options.C: Preventing severe acid reflux in a patient with a hiatal hernia
options.D: Placing a central venous line in the neck

explanation: Reverse Trendelenburg tilts the bed so the head is up, using gravity to keep stomach acid down where it belongs.

question: Which physical change points strongly to long-term high cortisol levels in Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Truncal obesity with thin extremities and a moon face
options.B: Rapid, unexplained weight loss accompanied by low blood pressure
options.C: Permanent darkening of the mucous membranes and gumlines
options.D: Severe generalized muscle wasting and profound skin darkening

explanation: Cortisol loves to move fat around—collecting it on the belly, back of the neck, and round face while making the arms and legs look thinner. You'll spot this look easily in practice!

question: Using the Plate Method for diabetes management, what should fill half of the dinner plate?

options.A: Full-fat dairy products
options.B: Starchy grains and yams
options.C: Lean protein foods
options.D: Non-starchy vegetables

explanation: Half of the plate should contain non-starchy vegetables to provide volume and fiber without raising blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h4)

question: What is the best nursing action when preparing a newly diagnosed patient for lifelong HIV treatment?

options.A: Providing clear, simple education on drug action, side effects, and adherence
options.B: Telling the patient to hide all pill bottles away from family members
options.C: Insisting that the patient stop working to focus entirely on health
options.D: Withholding information about side effects so the patient does not worry

explanation: You nailed it! Empowering patients with simple, honest education sets them up to manage their health with confidence.

question: Why are clear objectives important for a health facility?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nursing licenses
options.B: They ensure that nurses never have to work night shifts
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for hospital budgets
options.D: They prevent the facility from drifting and wasting resources

explanation: Without clear goals, a hospital or clinic loses its way. Clear objectives keep everyone focused so resources and energy aren't wasted.

question: When is a nurse most likely to use the rectal route of medication administration?

options.A: When the patient has severe vomiting and cannot swallow pills
options.B: When the patient prefers taking sweet liquids over tablets
options.C: When the drug is only available in a chewable tablet form
options.D: When the patient needs a slow-release oral multivitamin

explanation: Vomiting prevents oral medications from staying down, so the rectal route bypasses the upper gastrointestinal tract entirely. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h1)

question: Which specialist checks if a patient can swallow safely and recommends the right food textures?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Hospital pharmacist
options.C: Attending physician
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: Correct! Speech therapists are experts at testing swallow safety and helping prevent dangerous choking or aspiration.

question: Why is recent rectal surgery considered a strict contraindication for a flatus tube?

options.A: It disrupts healing surgical suture lines and causes injury
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: It permanently damages the anal sphincter muscles
options.D: It causes severe respiratory depression

explanation: Inserting a tube into a freshly operated rectum can tear fragile sutures, cause severe hemorrhage, and damage healing tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: How does poverty negatively affect the reproductive health of women in resource-limited settings?

options.A: It legally bars them from entering public health facilities
options.B: It guarantees that they will receive substandard care from international doctors
options.C: It prevents them from paying for transport, diagnostics, and essential medications
options.D: It automatically increases their biological fertility rate beyond normal levels

explanation: Out-of-pocket costs for transport, tests, and drugs are tough barriers that often force struggling women to miss out on the vital care they need.

question: Why do physical withdrawal symptoms happen when someone stops taking a drug suddenly?

options.A: The brain has forgotten how to produce natural energy
options.B: The digestive tract is rejecting leftover chemical toxins
options.C: The immune system is attacking the foreign drug molecules
options.D: The body has adapted to function with the drug present

explanation: Dependence means the bodily systems have shifted their baseline to accommodate the drug, causing distress when it is removed. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which piece of equipment attaches to the oxygen source to control gas flow into the tent?

options.A: Pulse oximeter
options.B: Flowmeter
options.C: Infusion pump
options.D: Suction canister

explanation: The flowmeter is your best friend for regulating the exact liters per minute of oxygen going into the tent system.

question: What does informed consent require before a nurse or doctor performs a reproductive health procedure?

options.A: The hospital management approves the procedure during a board meeting
options.B: The client understands the risks, benefits, and alternatives and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The head of the family gives written permission on behalf of the client
options.D: The local community leader signs a clearance certificate

explanation: Informed consent is an ethical requirement ensuring the patient is fully aware and willing without coercion. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which bacteria is most famous for causing fast, painful infections after a cat or dog bite?

options.A: Pasteurella multocida
options.B: Clostridium tetani
options.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Pasteurella lives happily in cat and dog mouths. Once introduced through a bite, it quickly causes sharp pain, redness, and swelling.

question: Why is the intraarticular route preferred for treating a single inflamed joint?

options.A: It prevents any risk of local infection at the injection site
options.B: It is completely painless compared to taking oral medications
options.C: It completely cures chronic arthritis after just one single dose
options.D: It delivers high drug concentrations directly to the target area with fewer systemic side effects

explanation: Targeting the joint directly keeps the medicine where it is needed most without flooding the entire body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: Where is the limbic system located in the brain?

options.A: Inside the hollow cavities of the cerebellum
options.B: At the very front tip of the frontal lobes
options.C: On the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.D: Deep inside the brain surrounding the brainstem

explanation: Spot on! The structures making up the limbic system sit deep inside, wrapping around the top of the brainstem right beneath the outer cortex.

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a refrigerator?

options.B: +2°C to +8°C
options.D: 0°C to +2°C

explanation: Most standard vaccines must be kept refrigerated within the +2°C to +8°C range to maintain their potency. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: Why is integrating family planning into primary healthcare centers important?

options.A: It removes the need for community health education programs.
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to work in large hospitals.
options.C: It ensures that even rural and remote communities can access services.
options.D: It makes contraceptive services exclusively available to the wealthy.

explanation: Primary health centers are right in the communities. Bringing family planning there means even folks in remote villages can easily get the care and advice they need.

question: Which of these is NOT a standard clinical quality indicator tracked in subacute facilities?

options.A: Development of new facility-acquired pressure injuries
options.B: Unplanned acute hospital readmission rates
options.C: Daily visitor parking satisfaction scores
options.D: Incidence of preventable medication administration errors

explanation: Correct! Parking is nice, but patient safety metrics like pressure sores, infections, and readmissions are what truly matter clinically.

question: Which factor can cause a pulse oximeter sensor to give an inaccurate reading on a patient's finger?

options.A: Cold fingers and poor peripheral circulation
options.B: Speaking in a normal tone of voice during the test
options.C: Drinking a glass of cold water before testing
options.D: A high room temperature on the hospital ward

explanation: Pulse oximeters rely on good blood flow through the finger; if circulation is sluggish or cold, the machine cannot read the pulse well. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: How do nurses check for pain or nerve issues in a baby who cannot talk yet?

options.A: Measure their daily weight gain
options.B: Ask parents to translate facial expressions
options.C: Check muscle electricity with a monitor
options.D: Look for constant crying and restlessness

explanation: Babies can't tell us where it hurts, so we watch their mood! Inconsolable crying and fussiness are their way of saying something is wrong.

question: What does a positive Babinski sign (toes fanning up) usually mean in an adult patient?

options.A: Normal peripheral nerve function
options.B: Dehydration and low blood pressure
options.C: Upper motor neuron damage
options.D: Severe vitamin deficiency

explanation: In babies, fanning toes are normal. But in adults, an upward Babinski reflex is a red flag pointing to upper motor neuron injury.

question: Which type of vitamin is most likely to cause toxicity if taken in excess because they store up in body fat?

options.A: Amino acid supplements
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins
options.C: B-complex vitamins
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fat and hang around in the body instead of being flushed out in urine. Too much of a good thing can be harmful!

question: In which care delivery model are duties divided strictly by tasks—like one nurse only giving medications and another only doing wound dressings?

options.A: Primary nursing
options.B: Functional nursing
options.C: Team nursing
options.D: Total patient care

explanation: Correct! Functional nursing focuses on getting specific tasks done across all patients, rather than assigning a whole patient to one nurse.

question: Which of these is a key sign of Conduct Disorder rather than Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD)?

options.A: Argues frequently with adult authority figures
options.B: Destruction of property and hurting animals
options.C: Blames others for their own mistakes
options.D: Loses temper easily when asked to clean

explanation: Conduct disorder involves severe violations of rules and laws, such as property destruction and physical aggression, which go beyond simple defiance.

question: What is a dangerous emergency complication for patients with high spinal cord injuries, often triggered by something simple like a full bladder?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.C: Malignant hyperthermia
options.D: Acute respiratory alkalosis

explanation: That's right! Autonomic dysreflexia causes a sudden, life-threatening spike in blood pressure triggered by discomfort below the injury, such as a full bladder or tight clothing.

question: What should you do immediately after a drain is successfully pulled out from a surgical wound?

options.A: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Leave the small hole open to the air so it dries quickly
options.C: Wash the open tract thoroughly with harsh antiseptic soap
options.D: Apply a sterile, airtight dressing over the insertion site

explanation: Always seal the site immediately with an airtight sterile dressing to protect the healing tissue and stop any air leaks or bleeding.

question: In the early days of medicine, what kind of products caused the very first cases of serum sickness?

options.A: Synthetic vitamins
options.B: Purified tap water
options.C: Animal-derived serum
options.D: Plant-based herbal teas

explanation: Back then, treatments used antibodies taken from animals (like horses), which human immune systems sometimes rebelled against.

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluating an IEC campaign?

options.A: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done exclusively by government auditors.
options.B: Monitoring happens after the campaign ends, while evaluation happens before printing.
options.C: Monitoring tracks distribution activities, while evaluation measures actual health outcomes and behavior changes.
options.D: Monitoring looks at money spent, while evaluation looks at paper quality.

explanation: Think of monitoring as tracking your daily steps during the campaign, while evaluation checks the final results and lifestyle changes at the end.

question: A study tests if a new low-salt diet lowers blood pressure in hypertensive patients. What is the independent variable?

options.A: The patient's blood pressure
options.B: The hospital reading room
options.C: The patient's age and weight
options.D: The low-salt diet

explanation: The independent variable is the intervention or action introduced by the researcher—in this case, the special diet.

question: What is the term for the bone tissue death in the hip or shoulder caused by blocked blood supply in sickle cell patients?

options.A: Avascular necrosis
options.B: Osteomyelitis
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Dactylitis

explanation: Avascular necrosis occurs when restricted blood flow deprives bone tissue of oxygen and nutrients, causing the bone to break down over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)

question: During a shift handover, which drug history detail is most critical to share?

options.A: The decorative color of the pill organizer brought from home
options.B: The brand name of the multivitamin taken once last year
options.C: Active high-risk medications like blood thinners and recent changes
options.D: The specific name of the retail pharmacy where drugs are bought

explanation: High-risk drugs require immediate team awareness during handovers to prevent severe adverse events. Excellent clinical judgment!

question: What is a major challenge when using wearable health devices in some Nigerian communities?

options.A: Excessive availability of high-speed fiber optic cables
options.B: Strict government bans on all digital wristwatches
options.C: A complete lack of patients suffering from chronic illnesses
options.D: Unstable electricity supply and limited internet connectivity

explanation: Frequent power cuts and poor network signals can sometimes make it tough to keep live health data syncing smoothly.

question: Which hospital team member is usually your go-to expert for helping a discharged patient find housing and food support?

options.A: The psychiatric social worker
options.B: The surgical floor pharmacist
options.C: The hospital laboratory technician
options.D: The institutional chief accountant

explanation: Spot on! Social workers are pros at connecting patients with community support, government programs, and welfare resources.

question: What is the core spiritual reason behind vegetarianism in many Hindu and Buddhist traditions?

options.A: Strict government mandates enforced by ancient rulers
options.B: Ahimsa, meaning non-violence toward all living creatures
options.C: The absence of livestock farming methods in early history
options.D: The belief that all animal proteins cause immediate physical disease

explanation: Ahimsa is the beautiful principle of avoiding harm to any living thing, which strongly guides plant-based eating habits in these traditions.

question: A patient is healing from major surgery. Which nutrient should you make sure they get more of to help their tissues repair?

options.A: Protein
options.B: Simple sugars
options.C: Saturated fats
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Spot on! Protein acts as the building blocks needed to fix cells, fight off infection, and rebuild damaged skin and muscles.

question: Which medical specialty focuses specifically on physical medicine and rehabilitation?

options.A: Neurology
options.B: Gerontology
options.C: Physiatry
options.D: Rheumatology

explanation: Physiatrists are the specialists who help patients rebuild their strength and function. Keep this term handy for your exams!

question: What is the very first logical step when planning a new community health campaign?

options.A: Evaluating final program results
options.B: Buying radio broadcast airtime
options.C: Printing colorful posters for clinics
options.D: Conducting a situational analysis

explanation: Before jumping into action, we always need to check the ground realities, culture, and specific needs of the community we want to help.

question: A nurse notices that outsourced lab staff keep missing deadlines, which delays patient medications. What is the best step for the nurse?

options.A: Perform all laboratory tests independently in addition to standard nursing duties
options.B: Ignore the delays because outsourced staff are outside the nursing department's control
options.C: Advise patients to purchase private insurance to get faster lab results
options.D: Document the delays and report them through proper administrative channels for contract review

explanation: As a patient advocate, document the facts clearly and report them up the administrative chain so management can fix the vendor issue.

question: Which of these is a direct medical cost in patient care?

options.A: Emotional distress experienced by family members
options.B: Hospital room charges and nursing care
options.C: Bus fare paid by a patient traveling to the clinic
options.D: Lost wages due to missing work while sick

explanation: Direct medical costs are the actual bills for clinical services and treatments—like your room, drugs, and nursing care.

question: Which position is most commonly used when giving an adult patient an enema?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: Supine position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Sims position

explanation: Sims is a side-lying position with the top leg bent. It gives you a safe, clear view and easy access to the rectum.

question: What chemical feature makes a fatty acid 'saturated'?

options.A: It only comes from plant sources
options.B: It stays completely liquid at room temperature
options.C: It has no double bonds between carbon atoms
options.D: It has multiple double bonds in the chain

explanation: Saturated fats are packed tightly together with single bonds only, which is why butter (a saturated fat) stays solid at room temperature!

question: What is the quickest, most reliable daily check to see if a patient is retaining fluid or losing too much?

options.A: Taking blood pressure every hour
options.B: Getting an accurate daily body weight
options.C: Checking the color of their fingernails
options.D: Checking how much food they ate

explanation: Think of it this way: a liter of fluid weighs about a kilo! Daily weights are your best tool to catch sudden fluid changes early.

question: What is a great way to improve vaccine turnout in a hesitant rural community?

options.A: Stopping all outreach visits and waiting for parents to find the clinic
options.B: Collaborating with respected local leaders and traditional rulers for health talks
options.C: Threatening parents with police arrest if they miss clinic appointments
options.D: Hiding the vaccine vials so people do not know what is being injected

explanation: Spot on! Traditional and community leaders have great influence and can help clear up rumors so families feel safe bringing their children.

question: Why are hospital-acquired infections a major concern for nurses using barriers?

options.A: Wards lack enough cleaning supplies
options.B: Hospital germs are easily spread to vulnerable patients
options.C: Patients bring all their own germs from home
options.D: Doctors rarely wash their hands

explanation: Sick patients in hospitals have lowered immune defenses, making them very easy targets for spreading germs if barriers are missed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a home health nurse?

options.A: Recognizing personal biases and respecting the patient's cultural beliefs
options.B: Ignoring cultural differences to treat everyone identically
options.C: Reading a textbook about a culture before every visit
options.D: Convincing the patient to adopt the nurse's personal lifestyle

explanation: It's all about checking your own biases at the door and keeping an open mind about how a patient's background shapes their health choices.

question: Which factor strongly influences a client's choice regarding contraceptive use?

options.A: The exact color of hospital waiting rooms
options.B: Cultural norms and religious beliefs
options.C: The brand of soap used in the clinic
options.D: Standard parking availability at the health center

explanation: Cultural expectations and religious traditions often guide what contraceptive methods are acceptable to a client and their family. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: How does making modern contraception easy for everyone to get help lower maternal death rates?

options.A: By shortening the normal physiological gestation period for women
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for emergency obstetric departments
options.C: By preventing all forms of sexually transmitted bacterial infections
options.D: By reducing the incidence of unintended pregnancies and unsafe abortions

explanation: Prevention is key! When people can easily access contraception, unplanned pregnancies drop, which means fewer people resort to dangerous, life-threatening unsafe abortions.

question: What is the best way to help prevent slips and falls in the bathroom?

options.A: Removing grab bars to increase arm movement
options.B: Applying heavy floor wax to make tiles shine
options.C: Placing non-slip mats on wet tub and shower surfaces
options.D: Turning off bathroom lights to reduce glare

explanation: Non-slip mats give great traction on slippery tiles when soap and water are around. It's a quick win for patient safety!

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Symptoms, Body, Analysis, Response
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Safety, Behavior, Action, Review
options.D: Staff, Bedside, Assessment, Report

explanation: SBAR provides a standardized, concise framework for sharing critical patient updates among health professionals. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h7)

question: Who is most likely to require custodial care over a long period?

options.A: An athlete recovering from a simple sports-related ankle sprain
options.B: A patient with a sudden bacterial infection needing a short antibiotic course
options.C: A person admitted to the emergency ward with acute appendicitis
options.D: An individual with chronic physical disabilities or severe cognitive loss

explanation: People with chronic disabilities or long-term cognitive decline often lose the ability to care for themselves independently, making custodial support necessary. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by PHC development committees in Nigeria?

options.A: Poor financial record-keeping
options.B: Lack of transport for community outreach
options.C: Excessive, surplus funding with no way to spend it
options.D: Political interference in local appointments

explanation: Committees almost always suffer from underfunding and resource scarcity rather than having too much money. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why do clinical wards need to do regular stock checks of their medicines?

options.A: To increase the speed at which pharmaceutical companies deliver orders
options.B: To prove to hospital management that nurses have extra free time
options.C: To ensure the medicine cupboards look neat and tidy for visitors
options.D: To catch and remove expired drugs before they reach patients

explanation: Regular checks help you spot expired or spoiling medicines early so patients never receive substandard care.

question: A hospital completely bans the use of a toxic chemical sterilizing agent and buys a safe machine instead. Which control strategy is this?

options.A: Administrative control
options.B: Work practice change
options.C: Elimination
options.D: Personal protection

explanation: Removing the toxic chemical completely from the facility means the hazard has been eliminated. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: A patient eating a full liquid diet after surgery suddenly gets severe stomach cramps and vomits. What should you do first?

options.A: Immediately upgrade the diet to solid foods
options.B: Encourage the patient to finish the meal quickly
options.C: Document the findings and ignore the symptoms
options.D: Pause the feeding and notify the surgical team

explanation: Correct! Cramping and vomiting mean the gut isn't ready yet. We need to stop the feeding and let the doctor know.

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a continuous supply of affordable essential drugs
options.B: To provide free medical care to all indigent citizens
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and buildings
options.D: To generate heavy profits for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF as a self-sustaining cycle. Its main job is to make sure essential drugs never run out in the hospital pharmacy, so patients can always get what they need at a fair price!

question: Which drug do we commonly use to boost weak contractions when there is no physical blockage?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Nifedipine
options.D: Dexamethasone

explanation: Brilliant! Oxytocin is our go-to medication because it mimics natural hormones to help the uterus contract more strongly.

question: Why is listening to parental concerns so critical during a nursing developmental assessment?

options.A: Parents can accurately prescribe educational therapies
options.B: Parents hold medical degrees that speed up diagnosis
options.C: Parents often notice subtle discrepancies in daily functioning first
options.D: Parents are legally required to sign all diagnostic tests

explanation: Caregivers spend the most time observing their children and frequently spot early behavioral or learning red flags before anyone else. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal benefit of well-funded disease-specific health programs?

options.A: Improved tracking and reporting of specific infectious disease outbreaks
options.B: Mass distribution of insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria
options.C: Expanded access to free antiretroviral medications for HIV patients
options.D: Complete elimination of all public health funding requirements for the national government

explanation: External aid is meant to support and supplement government efforts, not completely replace the nation's financial duty to its citizens.

question: What term describes the overlap between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Institutional friction
options.B: Operational burnout
options.C: Goal congruence
options.D: Budget deficit

explanation: 'Goal congruence' just means working in harmony—it's when your personal goals match up nicely with the hospital's goals.

question: Which of these is a classic life-saving action done during the primary survey?

options.A: Applying direct pressure to a severe hemorrhage
options.B: Administering a daily multivitamin tablet
options.C: Explaining hospital discharge policies
options.D: Scheduling a routine physical therapy appointment

explanation: Stopping massive bleeding right away is a critical life-saver to preserve circulation and prevent shock. Great clinical instinct!

question: You listen to all four areas of a patient's tummy for five full minutes and hear zero sounds. What does this mean?

options.A: Absent bowel sounds indicating decreased motility
options.B: Normal digestion happening very quietly
options.C: Mild gas trapped in the lower colon
options.D: Hyperactive sounds due to recent eating

explanation: Total silence for a full five minutes is a red flag! It usually means the intestines have slowed right down or stopped moving.

question: What is the main goal of holding a team nursing conference at the start of a shift?

options.A: To conduct formal examinations for student nurses
options.B: To review patient assignments and plan the shift together
options.C: To discuss hospital financial budgets
options.D: To discipline workers who came late to work

explanation: You got it! The brief conference helps the team connect, share updates, and organize duties so everyone knows what to expect before hitting the floor.

question: If a drug blocks L-type calcium channels in the heart, what happens?

options.A: Increased resting heart rate
options.B: Prolonged rapid ventricular firing
options.C: Immediate skeletal muscle paralysis
options.D: Decreased contraction strength

explanation: Less calcium getting in means less calcium released inside, which results in a weaker squeeze (lower contraction strength).

question: A pregnant patient refuses to eat meat because she heard it causes birth defects. How should you handle this as her nurse?

options.A: Force her to eat the meat immediately during the clinic visit
options.B: Scold the patient for believing foolish stories
options.C: Recognize this as a cultural myth and gently offer safe protein alternatives
options.D: Ignore her diet since beliefs have no impact on pregnancy

explanation: Always respect your patient's background! Providing gentle, accurate education and helping them find alternative protein sources builds great trust.

question: Why do modern nurses need to understand a bit of health economics?

options.A: To calculate daily patient medication dosages
options.B: To purchase personal medical equipment
options.C: To prove the financial value of professional care
options.D: To manage hospital pharmacy inventories

explanation: Knowing a bit of economics helps you stand up for your ward, justify why you need more hands on deck, and show management how vital nursing really is.

question: Why can a sudden infection mess up the results of a patient's blood protein test?

options.A: Infections trigger body changes that alter protein levels regardless of diet
options.B: Lab technicians are not allowed to run protein tests during an illness
options.C: Infections destroy all blood drawing needles in the clinic
options.D: Infection automatically cures any existing vitamin deficiency

explanation: Inflammation from an infection can drive blood protein levels down, which might trick you into thinking the patient is starving when they actually have an infection.

question: Why is working alongside local traditional and religious leaders vital when trying to stop harmful practices?

options.A: They are legally trained judges appointed to handle hospital disputes
options.B: They provide the funding needed to run modern surgical clinics
options.C: They are the only individuals permitted to perform nursing duties in villages
options.D: They hold significant influence and can help communities embrace positive cultural changes

explanation: Brilliant! When respected local leaders champion health education, community members are much more open to leaving harmful habits behind.

question: What is the main danger of leaving clear units of measurement off a bar chart's axis?

options.A: The hospital will fail to meet basic fire safety codes
options.B: The chart software will crash and delete the saved file
options.C: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed medications
options.D: Readers may misinterpret the data and make poor clinical decisions

explanation: Without clear units, nobody can tell if the numbers represent counts, percentages, or money. Always label your axes!

question: Which condition is a strict warning sign against doing a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Increased pressure inside the skull from a brain tumor
options.B: History of high blood pressure managed with pills
options.C: Mild dehydration from a recent stomach flu
options.D: A mild fever of 38 degrees Celsius with a headache

explanation: Spot on. Draining fluid when intracranial pressure is high can cause the brain to shift dangerously, which can be fatal.

question: Which section of a proposal summarizes the entire document and is usually written last?

options.A: Budget
options.B: Reference list
options.C: Methodology
options.D: Abstract

explanation: The abstract is a short summary that gives readers a quick overview of the whole proposal. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h3)

question: Where are parasympathetic terminal ganglia typically located?

options.A: Right next to the lateral sides of the spinal cord
options.B: Close to or inside the walls of target organs
options.C: Inside the sympathetic trunk chain along the spine
options.D: Directly within the white matter of the brainstem

explanation: Parasympathetic pathways have long preganglionic fibers because their ganglia sit near or inside the effector organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h5)

question: Which statement best describes informed consent in a longitudinal study?

options.A: It is an ongoing process that may need to be renewed as the study progresses
options.B: It is completely optional if the participants are hospital nurses
options.C: It is a one-time signature that never needs to be discussed again
options.D: It is only required on the very last day of data collection

explanation: Spot on! Because long studies evolve over time, participants should always remain informed and freely willing to continue.

question: Why is the hypodermis so important for protecting your bones and muscles?

options.A: It contains active stem cells that repair bone fractures
options.B: It acts as a physical shock absorber against trauma
options.C: It generates sweat to cool deep tissues during exercise
options.D: It produces keratin to harden the surface against impacts

explanation: Spot on! The layer of fat cushions bumps and blows, protecting the delicate muscles and bones underneath.

question: A woman with vasa previa goes into early labor and her water breaks. What is the biggest, most urgent danger to the baby?

options.A: Rapid fetal exsanguination from torn exposed vessels
options.B: Sudden maternal hypertension and stroke
options.C: Immediate maternal kidney failure
options.D: Complete placental abruption within seconds

explanation: Because a baby's total blood volume is so small, even a tiny tear in those unprotected blood vessels can lead to dangerous blood loss very quickly. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why are greenstick fractures much more common in young children than in adults?

options.A: Children have much higher calcium levels in their bones.
options.B: Children experience lower impact forces during play.
options.C: Children's bones lack a periosteum protective layer.
options.D: Children's bones are softer and more flexible.

explanation: Kids' bones are still growing, so they tend to bend and splinter on one side like a fresh green twig rather than snapping completely.

question: What is the main goal of mass casualty triage during a disaster?

options.A: Transporting all casualties directly to private tertiary hospitals
options.B: Providing immediate intensive care to every single injured person
options.C: Treating patients strictly in the exact order of their arrival
options.D: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people

explanation: When supplies and hands are limited, triage helps us make tough choices to save as many lives as possible.

question: In sickle cell disease, what causes red blood cells to bend into a crescent or 'sickle' shape?

options.A: Abnormal hemoglobin molecules
options.B: Low white blood cell counts
options.C: Excess dietary iron intake
options.D: Rapid platelet activation

explanation: Spot on! The hemoglobin inside the red blood cells has a slight structural change. When oxygen levels drop, these altered molecules stick together and pull the cell into that famous sickle shape.

question: What must a nurse do first before initiating any standing order protocol?

options.A: Contact the local government chairman to report clinic attendance
options.B: Conduct a thorough clinical assessment including history and vital signs
options.C: Ask the patient to sign a financial waiver for government services
options.D: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to cover all possible infections

explanation: A proper assessment provides the clinical evidence needed to decide whether a standing order applies to the patient's condition. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which heart rhythm do adults in sudden cardiac arrest show most often?

options.A: Atrial flutter
options.B: First-degree heart block
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Sinus bradycardia

explanation: In ventricular fibrillation, the lower chambers just quiver uselessly instead of pumping. Recognizing this rhythm is a key nursing skill!

question: How are wearable health trackers beginning to influence professional health records?

options.A: By replacing the need for licensed nurses in hospital wards
options.B: By serving as the primary billing invoice for insurance companies
options.C: By feeding real-time patient metrics directly into clinical systems
options.D: By automatically prescribing medications without a doctor's order

explanation: Wearables like smartwatches are starting to integrate live patient data such as heart rate and activity into medical records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h8)

question: Why do nurses and doctors use a standard classification system for FGM?

options.A: To help healthcare workers document and assess clinical needs
options.B: To assign legal penalties to specific practitioners
options.C: To determine the correct surgical reversal technique
options.D: To calculate the financial cost of hospital treatment

explanation: Exactly! Knowing the specific type helps nurses understand the patient's history and plan the best, most sensitive care possible.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to handle vaccine hesitancy from a caregiver?

options.A: Telling the caregiver that their personal beliefs are completely wrong
options.B: Listening respectfully to concerns and providing clear facts
options.C: Threatening to withhold other basic primary healthcare services
options.D: Ignoring the questions and quickly administering the injection anyway

explanation: You nailed it! Building trust through patience, empathy, and gentle education works way better than arguing or judging.

question: Why must nurses avoid typing patient-identifying details into public or unsecured search tools?

options.A: Search engines are unable to process medical words
options.B: The computer will instantly delete all nursing research files
options.C: Public search engines will charge the hospital a heavy fine
options.D: It violates patient data privacy and confidentiality ethics

explanation: Protecting patient identity is a core nursing duty, and entering identifiable health data into unsecured tools risks privacy breaches. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI)?

options.A: Reducing childhood mortality rates across the country
options.B: Protecting infants from vaccine-preventable infectious diseases
options.C: Completely eliminating all chronic genetic disorders in children
options.D: Building community immunity against dangerous pathogens

explanation: Correct! EPI focuses on infectious, vaccine-preventable diseases. Genetic disorders are inherited and aren't targeted by standard immunization vaccines.

question: What type of bowel prep is usually given right before a proctoscopy?

options.A: A 4-liter gallon prep
options.B: Total fasting for 48 hours
options.C: A cleansing enema
options.D: Oral magnesium citrate

explanation: Spot on! Because a proctoscopy only looks at the very end of the bowel, a quick cleansing enema just before the test is usually all it takes to clear the area.

question: In health informatics, what does the abbreviation CPOE stand for?

options.A: Certified Practical Operations Expert
options.B: Computerized Provider Order Entry
options.C: Central Pharmacy Order Exchange
options.D: Clinical Patient Online Evaluation

explanation: CPOE is just the digital system doctors and other providers use to type their orders directly into the computer network.

question: When planning a study, what exactly is a research design?

options.A: The overall structural blueprint for conducting a study
options.B: A detailed biography of the principal investigator
options.C: The final bibliography list at the end of a thesis
options.D: The statistical software used to type the report

explanation: Spot on! The research design is your master plan that guides you step-by-step from start to finish.

question: Why are teenagers often more prone to screen addiction than older adults?

options.A: Their prefrontal cortex is still maturing, making impulse control difficult
options.B: They have more financial resources to purchase high-end gadgets
options.C: They spend less time sleeping than adults do on average
options.D: Their eyes are more sensitive to the blue light emitted by screens

explanation: Think about brain development! The part of the brain that helps with self-control and good judgment is still growing in teens, making it harder to put the phone down.

question: Which brain chemical is most closely linked to psychotic symptoms?

options.A: Histamine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: You nailed it! Too much activity in the brain's dopamine pathways is a major factor in psychosis.

question: What should a nursing team do if their evaluation shows a new practice didn't improve patient results?

options.A: Hide the results from management so nobody gets blamed
options.B: Reassess how it was applied or look for alternative evidence
options.C: Stop all research activities in the hospital permanently
options.D: Keep using it anyway to avoid admitting any failure

explanation: Well thought out! Science is a journey of trial and learning. If it didn't work out, we review our steps or search for a better approach.

question: Why are financial assistance programs so important for many persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: They prevent extreme poverty caused by limited employment opportunities.
options.B: They replace the need for physical therapy and medical check-ups.
options.C: They cover all luxury expenses and travel costs.
options.D: They guarantee automatic employment in government ministries.

explanation: Financial grants act as a crucial safety net. Because physical disabilities can sometimes make finding stable jobs difficult, this aid helps prevent extreme hardship.

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you realize a medication error has reached a patient?

options.A: Assess the patient's clinical condition and notify the physician
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to see if any symptoms develop
options.C: Hide the empty medication wrapper inside your uniform pocket
options.D: Resign from your nursing position immediately out of guilt

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. Check on the patient right away and get the doctor's help to manage any unexpected reactions.

question: Which of these is NOT a reason why some families might hide a sick relative from home care providers?

options.A: Belief that family care is a strict moral obligation
options.B: Stigma associated with certain chronic or mental illnesses
options.C: Fear of community gossip and social judgment
options.D: Desire to follow strict hospital discharge protocols

explanation: Well done! Families might hide patients due to fear of gossip or stigma, but hospital protocols are never the reason.

question: What is the main job of the tiny hair-like cilia in your airways?

options.A: Absorb oxygen directly from inhaled air
options.B: Produce special chemicals to break down cell walls
options.C: Secrete thick mucus to trap foreign particles
options.D: Sweep trapped dust and germs upward and away from the lungs

explanation: Cilia use gentle, wave-like motions to push mucus and dirt up and out of your breathing tubes, keeping your lungs clean.

question: Which screening tool is best for catching lung cancer early in high-risk people who don't have symptoms yet?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
options.B: Standard routine sputum culture
options.C: Pulmonary spirometry test
options.D: Low-dose computed tomography scan

explanation: You've got this! A low-dose CT scan captures clear images of the lungs using very low radiation, making it the gold standard for high-risk screening.

question: What is the most common trigger for a vaso-occlusive pain crisis in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Taking daily folic acid supplements
options.B: Dehydration or infection
options.C: Eating high-protein meals
options.D: Sleeping on a firm mattress

explanation: Dehydration thickens the blood and infections increase physical stress, both of which easily trigger blood cells to sickle and block vessels. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a genogram during a family health assessment?

options.A: To track daily movement outside the neighborhood
options.B: To calculate the monthly food budget
options.C: To measure home square footage and ventilation
options.D: To map out inherited medical conditions and family history across generations

explanation: Think of a genogram as a medical family tree. It helps you quickly spot patterns of chronic illnesses like hypertension or diabetes.

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, immunity, and recovery
options.B: Source, symptom, and treatment
options.C: Vector, parasite, and climate
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: It's all about the agent causing the trouble, the host carrying it, and the environment bringing them together!

question: Why do nurses look beyond the obvious symptoms when a patient's condition is crashing?

options.A: To ensure the hospital billing department receives correct insurance data
options.B: Because lab technicians require secondary confirmation for all tests
options.C: So that family members can be discharged home earlier in the shift
options.D: Because primary organ failure quickly triggers a cascade affecting other systems

explanation: When one major organ starts failing, it quickly pulls other vital systems down with it. Checking the whole patient keeps you steps ahead!

question: What is a major economic benefit of educating women in developing communities?

options.A: Government taxes on local markets are completely abolished
options.B: Women earn higher incomes and contribute directly to poverty reduction
options.C: Men are relieved of all financial responsibilities in the household
options.D: Families stop spending money on food and agricultural supplies

explanation: Correct! Education opens doors to better jobs, allowing women to earn money that helps lift their whole household out of poverty.

question: Which environmental hazard is most commonly removed to prevent falls in a home care setting?

options.A: Solid dining tables
options.B: Heavy wooden wardrobes
options.C: Loose scatter rugs
options.D: Ceiling light fixtures

explanation: Loose rugs easily slip underfoot or catch walking aids, making them a major hazard for elderly clients with poor balance. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason a bag of blood must be completely infused within four hours?

options.A: To ensure the infusion pump battery does not run out of power
options.B: To prevent dangerous bacterial growth in the blood at room temperature
options.C: To stop the patient from becoming too cold during the procedure
options.D: To prevent the red blood cells from settling at the bottom of the bag

explanation: Blood is warm and rich in nutrients—bacteria love it too! Finishing it within four hours stops germs from multiplying in the bag.

question: What is the main root cause of inherited degenerative diseases that affect the brain?

options.A: Traumatic head injuries from physical accidents
options.B: Acute bacterial infections of the central nervous system
options.C: Genetic mutations passed down through families
options.D: Severe nutritional deficiencies in early childhood

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen because of faulty genes passed down in families, which slowly break down brain tissue over time. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h1)

question: What happens legally to a nurse who performs FGM in countries with strict anti-FGM laws?

options.A: They must pay a small fine for using hospital supplies
options.B: They are reassigned to administrative duties without penalty
options.C: They can face imprisonment and lose their nursing license
options.D: They receive a simple warning from the local health board

explanation: Laws target medical practitioners directly, imposing heavy legal penalties and revoking their right to practice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: What drives the private for-profit health sector?

options.A: Market forces and financial return
options.B: Universal free care mandates
options.C: Purely charitable donor funding
options.D: Strict government budget allocations

explanation: Private for-profit businesses rely on keeping their services running and sustainable through customer revenue and market demand.

question: To be most effective after an unprotected sexual assault, within how many hours should emergency contraception be given?

options.A: 120 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 12 hours
options.D: 48 hours

explanation: Well remembered! Emergency contraceptive pills work best when taken within 120 hours (or 5 days) after exposure.

question: Which of these options does NOT weaken or suppress a person's immune system?

options.A: Chronic high levels of physical and mental stress
options.B: Adequate daily nutrition and balanced diet
options.C: Severe protein and micronutrient deficiency
options.D: Long-term use of immunosuppressant medications

explanation: Nice work! Good food and a balanced diet nourish and support your immunity rather than harming it.

question: Why must hospital nurse managers align internal ward standards with national regulatory guidelines?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the emergency ward
options.B: To increase the private revenue of the nursing unit
options.C: To ensure legal compliance and maintain professional accountability
options.D: To bypass the need for hospital management approval

explanation: Internal rules must never fall below the legal minimums set by national regulatory bodies to protect patients and the institution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: Why is it necessary to use redundant communication systems during a disaster response?

options.A: Radio frequencies are too expensive for humanitarian groups
options.B: Paper notes are too heavy to carry around a disaster zone
options.C: Different agencies are legally banned from using mobile phones
options.D: Standard cellular networks and internet lines frequently collapse

explanation: Disasters routinely destroy power grids and cell towers, so teams need backup tools like satellite radios and runners. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why is it vital for hospitals to offer structured support programs for healthcare providers after adverse events?

options.A: To trick staff into admitting legal guilt so the hospital can fire them easily
options.B: To help clinicians process trauma and prevent long-term burnout or leaving the profession
options.C: To replace the need for conducting an actual Root Cause Analysis
options.D: To distract the public from noticing that a mistake occurred

explanation: Support programs protect staff well-being, helping them recover emotionally and continue providing safe care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h7)

question: When running health campaigns in Nigeria, who are considered key community gatekeepers?

options.A: Foreign aid organization directors
options.B: International travel agents
options.C: Private security guards
options.D: Traditional rulers and religious leaders

explanation: You nailed it! Traditional and religious leaders hold huge influence over local ways of life and are vital partners in winning the community's trust.

question: A surgical patient has a wound that is healing very slowly, even though they are eating enough daily calories. What is the most likely dietary culprit?

options.A: Excessive consumption of raw dietary fiber from fresh vegetables
options.B: Too many omega-3 fatty acids reducing the body's baseline temperature
options.C: Inadequate intake of high-quality protein and essential micronutrients
options.D: Drinking too much water instead of sweetened hospital beverages

explanation: Well done! Closing wounds and fighting off infection takes specific amino acids and vitamins. Without them, healing naturally slows down.

question: Why is a renal ultrasound often ordered when evaluating a patient with sudden kidney failure?

options.A: To test how well the liver is metabolizing circulating medications
options.B: To measure the exact amount of protein lost in a 24-hour period
options.C: To check for physical blockages or structural causes of urine backup
options.D: To determine the precise percentage of red blood cells in circulation

explanation: An ultrasound provides a clear image of the kidneys and urinary tract, helping doctors quickly identify postrenal obstructions like stones or an enlarged prostate. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h4)

question: What does a realistic healthcare plan take into account?

options.A: The personal hobbies of the hospital director
options.B: Architectural designs from foreign hospitals
options.C: International travel trends for medical tourists
options.D: Current staffing levels and available budget

explanation: A realistic plan matches its ambitions to what the facility can actually afford and staff right now.

question: What does the term 'phenomenology' mean in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: The genetic mapping of hereditary psychiatric traits
options.B: The physical lab tests used to check blood chemistry
options.C: The subjective, lived experience of the patient's symptoms
options.D: The mathematical chance of making a full recovery

explanation: Phenomenology is all about stepping into the patient's shoes to understand what their illness actually feels like from their own unique point of view.

question: What is a major focus when caring for a fistula patient BEFORE her surgery?

options.A: Applying heavy makeup to distract from the patient's visible sadness
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately after the initial medical diagnosis
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the bladder completely dry
options.D: Improving nutritional status and treating any active infections

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition helps tissues heal much faster, and clearing infections ensures the body is ready for surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: How does a slower kidney filtration rate affect drug safety in older adults?

options.A: It prevents oral medications from dissolving in the stomach
options.B: It forces all medications to be given through intravenous lines
options.C: It neutralizes the therapeutic effect of antibiotics instantly
options.D: It increases the risk of drug toxicity because drugs are cleared slower

explanation: Well reasoned! Since older kidneys filter blood more slowly, medications stay in the system longer and can build up to dangerous levels if doses aren't adjusted.

question: Two clinical nurses independently score a patient's wound healing using the same chart. What type of reliability are they testing?

options.A: Parallel forms reliability
options.B: Test-retest reliability
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Internal consistency reliability

explanation: Since two separate raters are checking their agreement on the same patient, it's inter-rater reliability in action!

question: Which type of care home offers short-term stays to give family caregivers a quick break?

options.A: Nursing care
options.B: Respite care
options.C: Dementia care
options.D: Palliative care

explanation: Brilliant! Respite care gives family members a much-needed temporary break by stepping in to handle care duties for a short while.

question: What is a major immediate health risk associated with sexual violence?

options.A: Permanent loss of hearing capacity due to psychological shock
options.B: Sudden elevation of red blood cells in the circulatory system
options.C: Acquisition of sexually transmitted infections and unwanted pregnancy
options.D: Immediate development of chronic osteoarthritis in the knees

explanation: Sexual assault places victims at immediate risk for physical trauma, sexually transmitted infections, and unwanted pregnancies requiring emergency prophylaxis. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h4)

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain ramps up electrical activity during a seizure?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Glutamate

explanation: Spot on! Glutamate is the main 'gas pedal' neurotransmitter that drives excessive brain cell firing during a seizure.

question: What molecule builds up inside muscle cells to help them relax when a beta-2 agonist is used?

options.A: Cyclic AMP (cAMP)
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Calcium ions
options.D: Phosphodiesterase

explanation: When beta-2 agonists do their magic, they boost cAMP levels inside the cell, which tells the muscle to relax and let go of the tightness.

question: Why does a baby facing forward (occiput posterior position) often cause a long labour?

options.A: It softens the cervix too early before contractions even begin.
options.B: It forces a wider diameter of the fetal head to fit through the pelvic dimensions.
options.C: It immediately causes the placenta to detach from the uterine wall.
options.D: It completely stops the mother from breathing deeply during contractions.

explanation: Well done. When the baby's head faces the mum's tummy instead of her back, it cannot squeeze through the pelvis as easily, causing a traffic jam!

question: Why is self-care considered an absolute must for mental health nurses, rather than just a nice bonus?

options.A: Unmanaged burnout and fatigue can impair clinical judgment and compromise patient safety
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to log relaxation hours for promotion
options.C: Patients refuse care from nurses who look tired
options.D: It is the only way to avoid ever working night shifts

explanation: You cannot pour from an empty cup! Looking after your own mental health keeps your clinical judgment sharp so you can keep your patients safe.

question: Why is long-term evaluation so important in Behaviour Change Communication?

options.A: It proves that the nurse worked extra hours without taking a break
options.B: It measures whether actual health practices were sustained over time
options.C: It allows the hospital to increase consultation fees for patients
options.D: It replaces the need for daily clinical nursing assessments

explanation: You nailed it! Real habit changes take time. Long-term checks let you know if the community kept up the healthy lifestyle weeks or months later.

question: Why is teaching job skills (vocational training) so helpful in rehab programs for recovering users?

options.A: It replaces the need for any prescription medications during detox
options.B: It guarantees they will pass all school board examinations
options.C: It equips them with economic skills to rebuild their lives after treatment
options.D: It legally prevents them from ever feeling stressed again

explanation: Giving recovering individuals a way to make an honest living helps prevent poverty and unemployment, which often cause relapse. Brilliant!
